traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Rosa (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.54 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 54 records in 5 sources); trunks 0.55, branches 0.54. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Rosa by W. H. Lewis, B. Ertter and A. Bruneau (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs or subshrubs of 1 to 20 stems, often spreading by rhizomes or stolons; leaves alternate on the stems, deciduous (rarely kept), pinnate with (3-)5-11(-13) leaflets, the side ones nearly stalkless and the end one stalked, so the leaf ends in a leaflet; stems armed with prickles grown from the skin (paired or single below the stipules, others between the nodes), rarely unarmed; petals 5, their tips usually notched; stamens 35-220; the fruit a hip, achenes gathered inside the fleshy hypanthium.

traits.stem_clump.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Rosa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 1-20 stems, rhizomatous or stoloniferous, so usually a clump of many stems, often a thicket; each species' account says which.

traits.spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Rosa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): the genus's prickles and aciculi are outgrowths of the stem's skin, not thorns; a few species have stems nearly unarmed.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Rosa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences terminal, usually on the lateral branches, sometimes on the main stems and shoots.
